ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown, it is known that $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle ADE$ are both isosceles right-angled triangles, with $\angle BAC=\angle ADE=90^\circ$, and $AB=AC=1$, $AD=DE=\sqrt{5}$. Point D lies on line BC, and the extension of line segment $EA$ intersects line BC at point F. What is the length of $FB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw AH $\perp$ BC at point H,\\
$\because$ $\angle$BAC=$90^\circ$, AB=AC=1,\\
$\therefore$ BC=$\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\because$ AH$\perp$BC,\\
$\therefore$ BH=CH=$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ AH=$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\because$ AD=DE=$\sqrt{5}$,\\
$\therefore$ DH=$\sqrt{AD^{2}-AH^{2}}=\sqrt{5-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$,\\
$\therefore$ CD=DH−CH=$\sqrt{2}$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$ABC=$\angle$ACB=$45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$ABF=$\angle$ACD=$135^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$DAE=$45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$DAF=$135^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$BAC=$90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$BAF+$\angle$DAC=$45^\circ$,\\
$\because$ $\angle$BAF+$\angle$F=$45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle$F=$\angle$DAC,\\
$\therefore$ $\triangle$ABF$\sim$ $\triangle$DCA,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{AB}{CD}=\frac{BF}{AC}$,\\
$\therefore$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{BF}{1}$,\\
$\therefore$ BF=$\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$.
